I see activists in various domains being criticized for this reason : them being part - to some extent - of the very thing they are protesting. This is seen as a justification of the fact that their actions have no true value. How do you feel about that ?

Here are some examples :

  • Can an environmentalist protest against oil drilling in the Arctic and drive to the protest in a car ?
  • Can an activist protesting sweat-shops in China own a smartphone ?
  • Can a neo-luddite be against modern technology and have an email account ?
  • Can a film maker produce a TV ad for the DVD of his Anti-consumerism documentary ?

You get it, can you genuinely protest a system while being a part of it ?
Can you be against something you are a part of ?

I think it's possible to protest a system while being a part of it. In many cases, there is no reasonable alternative than to participate in the very system you're protesting. I believe many people that protest a system in which they participate, are protesting the way the system is run, not necessarily the existence of the system. A film maker producing a TV ad for the DVD of his anti-consumerism documentary, may need to make viewers aware that proceeds from the sale of the DVD would go towards actual change in consumerist policy.

I think it's possible to protest certain taxation codes while still abiding by the tax code. To not participate would be illegal and for many people who do not wish to go to jail or prison, non-participation is not a feasible option. Many people who protest banks are still forced to rely upon their services as there may not be many if any good alternatives.

Your examples seem "all or nothing" and I don't think anything worth protesting is always as easy as that.

At the same time, I think it's fair to criticize activists that participate in the systems they protest. Criticism can and should force activists to re-evaluate why they are protesting and hopefully build a better foundation for the reasons and merits of their protests. If people are not challenged in their beliefs, real change would be hard to accomplish in my opinion.

I think that you can, as many of these things may be considered necessary. The documentary may be good, but without ads it wouldn't reach many and thus wouldn't be that useful. Sometimes, not partaking even indirectly in something you are against is too much of a sacrifice, so you use it more effective. Your smartphone may have been made in a sweatshop by an almost slave, but if you manage to get people to support humane conditions thanks to a #hashtag it would be worth it.
